etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English creatour, from Old French creator, creatur, creatour, from Latin creātor, agent noun from perfect passive participle creātus (“created”), from verb creō (“I create”) + agent suffix -or. Mostly displaced native Old English wyrhta (modern English wright).

definitions.definition: Something or someone which creates or makes something.
(social media) Ellipsis of content creator, someone who regularly produces and publishes content on social media, especially of a monetizable nature.

quote.citation: 2021 May 4, Taylor Lorenz, “Mr. Beast, YouTube Star, Wants to Take Over the Business World”, in The New York Times‎[1], →ISSN:
quote.text: People have viewed his videos more than 13 billion times. And last year as the pandemic raged, he became the most-subscribed YouTube creator in the country.

quote.citation: 2022 July 14, Rafqa Touma, “Melbourne woman ‘dehumanised’ by viral TikTok filmed without her consent”, in The Guardian‎[2]:
quote.text: The video shows TikTok creator Harrison Pawluk approaching the woman, Maree, in a public shopping centre.

definitions.definition: (religion, sometimes capitalized) The deity that created the world.
(sports) A player who creates opportunities for their team to score goals; a playmaker.

quote.citation: 2019 July 3, Andrea Canales, Jonathan Tannenwald, “Pulisic, McKennie show plenty of promise for U.S. in Gold Cup”, in The Philadelphia Inquirer‎[3]:
quote.text: Hernández is not a creator and suffered from a lack of service in previous seasons.

quote.citation: 2022 October 13, Richard Jolly, “Record-breaker Mohamed Salah delivers timely reminder of his greatest strength ahead of clash with champions”, in Independent.ie‎[4]:
quote.text: There have been times this season when it seemed Liverpool were trying to reinvent Salah, the scorer supreme, as a creator and this was a sudden reminder of his greatest strength.

quote.citation: 2022 October 19, Andre Snellings, “Fantasy basketball: Why Jalen Brunson can be even better in New York”, in ESPN‎[5]:
quote.text: As such, when Doncic was on the court, Brunson was a secondary facilitator and more of a finisher than a creator.
